paragraphs: Markets over the last day: the eight tracked equity indices moved +0.38% on average, with Nikkei 225 strongest (+1.94%) and Euro Stoxx 50 weakest (-0.45%). Brent crude changed -4.03% to 98.46. Gold changed +0.80% to 4,213.2002. Bitcoin changed +0.33% to 83,899.3281. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.249%, a relative move of -0.11%. Among the firms tracked, Freeport-McMoRan (+3.40%) and US Oil Fund (ETF) (+2.54%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: Shein shares sink after profits disappoint in first results since IPO (FT Markets). Fast-fashion retailer squeezed by rising freight costs and Iran war fallout Deals and capital markets: FirstFT: Anthropic IPO filing warns of ‘existential risks’ (FT Companies). Also in today’s newsletter: oil bonds link and Rubio says ‘foreign actor’ behind UK terror plot Central banks and macro: Inflation accelerates in Eurozone’s biggest economies (FT World). Faster-than-expected consumer price growth could increase pressure on the ECB to raise rates Central banks and macro: A warning of ‘breakdowns and deficiencies’ in security at the US central bank (FT World). Also in today’s newsletter, Marco Rubio blames ‘foreign actor’ for UK terror plot and US completes Iraqi troop withdrawal Geopolitics and trade: Middle Eastern oil exports rise to highest level since Iran war began (FT Markets). Shuttle services through Strait of Hormuz have brought shipments to more than 80% of prewar daily average
